clue.text: Legalist holding back food for livestock

indicators.note: going back means the hidden run of letters is read from right to left
a word holding something keeps it inside, so the answer sits within the letters of the previous word

parts.note: the letters in the middle of this word, read in printed order

explanation.surface: A rule-obsessed official is withholding animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the middle of lEGALISt backwards to get SILAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented green fodder stored in a silo for feeding cattle and sheep over winter.

clue.text: Caustic Rita's back in charge

indicators.note: turned back means the name and its possessive ending are read from right to left

parts.note: the name with its possessive s
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued Rita has returned to run things.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiric writing or speech is biting and mocking, which is what caustic describes.

clue.text: Release constructive toy — about time!

indicators.note: about means going around, so the brand name wraps around the letter for time

parts.note: Lego is the plastic building-brick toy
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A parent finally gets the building-brick set out of the box.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to stop holding it, which is to release it.

clue.text: Hans Christian Andersen's dog?

parts.note: surface reading: the pet kept by the famous writer of fairy tales
setter's reading: Andersen himself was a celebrated Dane, and a large dog breed is named after that nationality

explanation.walkthrough: Andersen, the author of The Little Mermaid, was Danish and famous, so he was an eminent Dane; the question mark flags the pun on the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed of dog, and Andersen was a distinguished man from Denmark.

clue.text: Possibly trump one on account of heart

parts.note: a trump is one example of a playing card
the Roman numeral for one
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A bridge player trumps out of passion rather than strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the account abbreviation after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the medical adjective relating to the heart, as in cardiac arrest.

clue.text: Medical man from Prague heard on high

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the word for the person rather than its spelling

parts.note: a man from Prague is a Czech, which is pronounced like a word meaning inspection
on high means up

explanation.surface: A Czech doctor is overheard somewhere above.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical, as a noun, is a routine examination by a doctor, which is the same as a checkup.

clue.text: Argument to continue at home

parts.note: to run is to continue, as a play runs for months
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to keep a quarrel going inside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or confrontation, especially with authority, so it is an argument.

clue.text: In going to war, Neil developed foot problem

indicators.note: something that has developed has changed form, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: all sixteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier called Neil picks up a painful foot complaint on his way to battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail growing into the flesh of the toe is a common and painful condition of the foot.

clue.text: Vessel for wine from a service in church

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written
the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Communion wine comes from a vessel used at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a religious service, but it is an armed service, the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open glass flask in which wine or water is served at table.

clue.text: Foolish chap with extremely effeminate beard

parts.note: a goat is slang for a silly person, as in acting the goat

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A silly man sports a rather dainty bit of facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard on the chin, named for its likeness to a goat's.

clue.text: Right function for Othello, say

parts.note: a title is a legal right or entitlement, as to property
a role is a function someone performs

explanation.surface: Someone asks which job suits Othello properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the part that gives Shakespeare's play its name, an example of a title role.

clue.text: African country's troubled reign

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the letters of the following word are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A country in Africa is going through an unsettled rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked republic in West Africa, named after the river that crosses it.

clue.text: Sleeping place for bounder on street

parts.note: a kangaroo, or roo, bounds along
ST is the abbreviation for street, placed on, after, the animal

explanation.surface: A cad is looking for somewhere to sleep on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is old British slang for a cad, but here it is something that literally bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the perch or place where birds settle to sleep.

clue.text: Beginning (or ending) imitation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plane ... is beginning its flight, and ... a day ends work early

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket plays on the phrase meaning both launching into the air and removing or stopping something.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off is both lifting off or starting suddenly and doing a mocking impression of somebody.

clue.text: Within Institute there's money to burn

indicators.note: within puts the money abbreviation inside the word for institute as a verb

parts.note: to institute something is to establish or create it
M is a common abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A rich institution has cash to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institute' looks like a noun, a college, but it is a verb meaning set up; 'money to burn' is a phrase the clue splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate a body is to burn it to ashes.

clue.text: Curious men short of money, requiring first couple to leave

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for money is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for money

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word must go away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nosy men, broke, are being asked to leave as the first pair to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop M from MEN and RE from REQUIRING to give EN + QUIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: An enquiring mind is inquisitive and eager to learn, which is what curious means.

clue.text: Father's thirty, oddly affected by advancing years

parts.note: pa is father, followed by the possessive s

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the number word

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Dad has turned thirty and is feeling his age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to do what they once could, worn down by the years.

clue.text: Maybe Ruby's cut flower

parts.note: a ruby is an example of a precious stone
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruby has snipped a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby with a capital R looks like a name; it is the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a low succulent plant, a sedum, bearing small star-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Turn informer, finding queen in clinch

indicators.note: in puts the queen's letter inside the word for an embrace

parts.note: to clinch a deal is to seal it
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Someone grassed after finding the queen locked in an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal is slang for informing on accomplices to the police.

clue.text: During vague illness, appeal for regular form of service

indicators.note: during places the word for appeal inside the word for the vague illness

parts.note: the lurgy is British slang for an unspecified minor illness
it means sex appeal, as in she's got it

explanation.surface: While feeling under the weather, someone asks for a routine church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is the fixed set form of public worship used in a church.

clue.text: Baronet interrupted by unrefined bore

indicators.note: a thing interrupted by something has that something break into its middle

parts.note: BT is the abbreviation for baronet
rough means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman is cut short by a coarse, tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore and brought are both past tenses of verbs for carrying, as in she bore or brought gifts.

clue.text: Deprived fellow in flat cap

indicators.note: in puts the letter for fellow inside the kind of hat

parts.note: a beret is a soft flat round cap
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A poor man stands in his flat cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means having been robbed or deprived of something, often a loved one.

clue.text: See 6
One caught in sting gets something to calm the stomach

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of letters inside the word for sting

parts.note: a barb is a sharp point or a stinging remark
the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a police sting is handed an antacid.
explanation.walkthrough: I and C go inside BARB, splitting it as B-IC-ARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarb, sodium bicarbonate, neutralises stomach acid and is a home remedy for indigestion.

clue.text: He causes dreadful irritation right away

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so the remaining letters are jumbled
away means removed, so one letter for right is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A troublemaker stirs up terrible annoyance immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as immediately; it means remove one R from the fodder before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiator is the person who sets something going, so he causes it to happen.

clue.text: Turn up missing volume, showing no reaction

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for volume is left out

parts.note: to invert is to turn upside down
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Someone turns up the sound and gets no response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like arrive or increase; read it as overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: An inert substance, like a noble gas, does not react chemically with others.

clue.text: Standard well below par

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the figure of an ... carried as a Roman legion's standard
second meaning: in golf, a score of two strokes under par for a hole

explanation.walkthrough: 'well below par' sounds like poor quality, but in golf below par is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman legions marched behind an eagle emblem, and golfers call a hole played two under par by the same bird name.

clue.text: Individual stabs King George — he's had it

indicators.note: something that stabs is driven into the middle of what follows

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A lone assassin knifes the monarch, who is done for.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is a person who is doomed or beyond saving, someone who has had it.

clue.text: Armies primarily approve of uniform

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter
to like something is to approve of it

explanation.surface: Military forces mainly endorse a standard dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like military clothing; it is the adjective meaning the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are alike are identical or similar throughout, which is what uniform means as an adjective.

clue.text: Judge taking long time about final polls

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for long time goes around the word for final

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A judge spends ages over the last round of voting.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on a single question, so they are polls; the Latin plural matches the plural noun.

clue.text: Great effort to conceal old hatred

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so the letter for old goes within

parts.note: big means great in size
a try is an attempt or effort
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to hide a long-standing grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great effort' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces, with the letter for old tucked between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerant prejudice towards others, a kind of hatred for those who differ.

clue.text: Continuous decline left Paris reeling

indicators.note: reeling means staggering about, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A long slump has left the French capital staggering.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral is a steady worsening that feeds on itself, as in a downward economic spiral.
